title: Part 5
html:
Sandhitirtha, the Kaveri, Nagar. Tanjore. Padmakot and the healing of the blind man. Tripatra and the Shaiva Bharga. The great forest. Srirangam and the brahmana who reads the Gita (pp. 81–100)

[p. 81]

878There the two rivers Nanda and Bhadra meet;
going there, he bathed at their confluence.

879The master of that tirtha is Sadananda Puri;
he turned out to be a very learned pandit.

880Sadananda Puri raised the doctrine of advaita,
but with a single argument the Lord broke all Puri's pride.

881In the end Sadananda, amazed,
fell rolling at the Lord's feet in a surge of devotion.

882Having given him the truth of devotion, my sannyasi
went to Chaipalla-tirtha to see its ways.

883The dwellers of that tirtha are very virtuous;
there the sannyasi, son of Shachi, arrived.

884There was a beautiful bhairavi1 named Siddheshvari,
radiant, a great ascetic, like Maheshvari herself.

885From austerities she was nothing but skin and bone;
she sat at the foot of a bilva tree, repeating her mantra.

886She sat motionless, absorbed in meditation;
seeing her, a sinner gains much knowledge.

887She had reached a hundred years of age,
yet no one could tell it from her appearance.

888There was another, a bhairavi named Shrigali;
she lived on the bank of the river.

[p. 82]

889Having reverently seen Shrigali,
the son of Shachi went on to the bank of the Kaveri.

890Having bathed in the Kaveri, young Gauranga
became lost in drinking the nectar of the Name of Hari.

891In the afternoon he told me to go begging,
and I went into the town for alms.

892Collecting a little parched grain and flour,
I brought them and set them before the Lord.

893The Lord made rotis and offered the bhoga,
and on receiving the prasada I was refreshed.

894My merciful Lord, in the town of Nagar,
rose in the morning and went on, full of love for Krishna.

895Smeared with dust, hair matted, with no other talk,
Nimai goes along the road saying "Krishna, Krishna".

896In the town of Nagar there are Sri Rama and Lakshmana;
going there, the Lord bowed to them.

897Many people live in Nagar,
and there he made the Name of Hari manifest.

898Seeing the movement of the Lord's love, the townsfolk,
from children to women, all turned from worldly things.

899For three days he sang and danced there,
and the news of it spread from town to town.

[p. 83]

900People gathered from ten kroshas around,
and one by one the Lord gave them all the Name of Hari.

901Never have I seen so merciful a Lord:
Chaitanya Gosai gives the Name from house to house.

902There was a wicked brahmana there;
calling the Lord a fraud, he tried to drive him away.

903That brahmana thakura with his gang
shouted at the merciful Lord, "Away, away, away!"

904The brahmana thakura said, "You cheat!
Dressed up as a false sannyasi, you're making trouble!

905On the pretext of religious teaching you are ruining the village people.
I'll expose you and drive you out this very minute!"

906He came before the Lord and heaped abuse on him,
and the Lord laughed his harsh words away.

907At last Chaitanya Gosai called the brahmana
and said, "Beat me, brother, but say 'Hari'."

908All the other people who were around him,
seeing the brahmana's behaviour, rushed to beat him.

909Merciful Chaitanyadeva, reflecting,
began to speak to the brahmana, addressing him:

910"Listen, merciful brahmana thakura:
say 'Hari, Hari' and you will find great happiness.

[p. 84]

911In this transient body there is no happiness;
sink yourself in the Name of Hari and rejoice, brother.

912This body is an inert lump; at the time of death
no one will go with you — this is certain.

913Brothers, friends, wife, sons — no one belongs to anyone;
all of them are clothes, ornaments and heaps of money.

914Jackals and dogs will eat the transient body;
it will rot and decay — be sure of this.

915Raise your arms, say 'Hari' and dance with me,
and you will never again have to go to Yama's abode.

916Wife or son — it is a juggler's game,
a gathering in the world for a couple of days.

917The family plays tricks for the sake of food.
Think, brother: who is who to you?

918Throwing the noose of love round his neck, the woman pulls hard,
and by that pull the foolish master of the house dies.

919Sweet words on her lips and poison in her heart;
when she gets no money, she grinds her teeth.2

920She never lets him take the path of truth;
she binds him in bonds and destroys all his aspirations.

921A woman's love is like poison,
yet the fool drinks it, calling it nectar.

[p. 85]

922At the hour of death sons and daughters come near
and say, 'Father, what have you left for us?'

923Think of all this, good brother brahmana,
and say 'Hari' with devotion — this is the alms I beg.

924Strike me — that is no sorrow;
say 'Hari' with all your heart — this is the alms I beg.

925Say 'Hari' with devotion; the Name will go with you,
and through it you will gain eternal happiness for endless time."

926All the people who stood around
grew excited at the Lord's words.

927Crying "Hari bol!", they all began to dance,
and the heart of the unbelieving brahmana was purified.

928By the Lord's grace the brahmana grew drunk with the Name of Hari
and fell to the ground at the Lord's feet.

929Thus having blessed the brahmana,
Chaitanyadeva left Nagar.

930As he set out, the best of sannyasis
signalled me to get up quickly.

931I tied the two pairs of sandals onto my head
and took the two loads on my two shoulders.

932How many respectable women ran to see the Lord!
He went on to the town of Tanjore, seven kroshas away.

[p. 86]

933In Tanjore lives a Vaishnava brahmana
named Dhaleshvara, who serves Krishna.

934In his temple there are images of Radha and Krishna,
and there my Gora went slowly.

935In the middle of the brahmana Dhaleshvara's courtyard
stands a huge bakula tree in its splendour.

936Many Vaishnava sannyasis live there;
whoever sees that place, even a householder, becomes detached.

937To its left is the Shiva Gosamaja;
the Lord had darshan of Shiva with love.

938Nearby was a delightful lake,
and the brahmana Dhaleshvara showed him the way.

939The lake is at Kumbhakarna-kapara;3
seeing it, the Lord was amazed.

940Near it is a hill called Chandalu,
standing as if painted on a canvas.

941All round it are many caves,
where many sannyasis live to practise austerities.

942How many sannyasi gosais, absorbed in meditation,
sit with closed eyes and ash-smeared bodies!

943There an excellent brahmana named Bhatta
took the Lord to his own house.

[p. 87]

944Hearing the name of Krishna, the brahmana went mad,
and merciful Chaitanya bestowed his grace on him.

945The worthy Bhatta is always drunk with the Name of Hari;
when he takes Krishna's name, tears fall.

946Seeing his ecstasy of love, beautiful Gauranga
said, "Brahmana, you are the best of sadhus.

947Seeing you, even great sins are destroyed.
You, worthy brahmana, are my master;

948seeing you, no sorrow or suffering remains."
At the praise the brahmana was deeply ashamed,

949and he ran and fell at the Lord's feet.
He said, "Lord, why do you embarrass me so?

950Words of praise only increase this wretch's pain.
I am a worm of hell, the crest-jewel of sinners;

951you yourself have saved me by your grace.
Whoever touches me goes to hell;

952today by your grace my sins are destroyed."
Seeing the brahmana's humility, the son of Shachi

953said, "Brahmana, you are blessed, you are a holy man."
In an ecstasy of love the Lord dances in the brahmana's house,

954and seeing it the brahmana rejoices at heart.4

[p. 88]

955There was a chief sannyasi named Sureshvara
who served Hari unceasingly.

956Six others were under him;
all of them, detached, worship in the forest.

957Huge trees stand in splendour all around;
the wondrous beauty of that forest is beyond words.

958In the middle of that forest is a little river,
most charming, flowing with a murmuring sound.

959The waters of the springs all join together
and become a river cutting through the forest.

960There they all live and go nowhere,
and the village people bring them alms there.

961That lovely place is a great holy land,
and there Mahaprabhu went on.

962Seeing the Lord, that detached sannyasi
thrilled with joy, floating in bliss.

963Gora Raya stayed there for some days,
and, drunk with bliss, sang the glories of Hari.

964Then the sannyasi Sureshvara, amazed,
danced with the Lord, floating in the waters of love.

965That place is in the kingdom of King Jaysingh;
the king takes no tax from sannyasis.

[p. 89]

966That place is like the abode of Vaikuntha;
when one enters it, the heart is soothed.

967Leaving that forest, the son of Shachi
went on to see the tirtha of Padmakot.

968The goddess of Padmakot is the eight-armed Bhagavati;
going there, the Lord bowed down to her.

969My Gora Raya sang many hymns,
and hundreds of people ran to see him.

970Sitting there, the Lord gave teachings,
and hundreds of people gathered there.

971The Lord said, "Brothers, all of you chant the Name of Hari;
by the power of the Name, brothers, you will all reach the eternal abode.

972Tell me, what need is there of the inert body?
When you die, jackals and crows will eat it.

973All of you have fallen into the net of maya;
tear the net, brothers, by chanting the Name of Hari.

974Whose daughter, whose son — all a false pretence;
saying 'mine, mine', everyone has lost his senses.

975Whose are you, who is yours, who is kin and who a stranger?
Maya is playing like a juggler.

976Those who harbour worldly desires in this world

[p. 90]

suffer much torment, coming and going.

977In the womb they live among excrement
and satisfy their cravings by eating faeces and urine.

978Those who take the inert body to be consciousness —
how will they get out of hell?

979Those who take the part for the whole
dwell forever in hell.

980Not knowing that worldly life is a cruel trap,
people fall into that trap and suffer much grief.

981The soul has no death; the sinful body dies.
Yet, deluded and enchanted by maya, the creature loves the body."

982At this teaching everyone was amazed,
and the eight-armed goddess seemed to tremble.

983As soon as the cry of "Hari" came from Lord Chaitanya's lips,
at once an echo rang out all around.

984Boys, girls and young men went wild,
and the eight-armed goddess seemed to sway.

985The fragrance of lotus began to waft all around,
and suddenly a rain of flowers fell there.

986All the women threw flowers,
playing with flowers out of devotion.

987There was a blind holy man there;
with devotion he clasped the Lord's feet.

[p. 91]

988The Lord said, "Let me go, best of sadhus."
The blind man said, "Have mercy, Lord of the world."

989The Lord said, "The Lady of the world is here."5
The blind man said, "Have mercy on the wretched, Hari.

990Have mercy on me, merciful Lord;
my heart weeps because I cannot see your form.

991I am a blind wretch; I cannot see.
Show me your form, Chaitanya Gosai."

992The Lord said, "You have no fleshly eyes,
but with the eye of knowledge you see everyone's heart.

993The ignorant see with their eyes;
the wise see everything with eyes closed.

994You are that wise one, worthy blind man;
I believe you see everything within."

995The blind man said, "Why do you play tricks, treasury of compassion?
Have mercy on me as a blind man; you are Bhagavan.

996For many years I have been lying in the temple,
and in a dream Bhagavati made it clear to me.

997You are that Bhagavan, the refuge of the helpless —
so Bhagavati told me in a dream.

998Then I shall know you, merciful one,
if you show your form to the blind.

[p. 92]

999The feet of an ant uproot mountains,
the lame cross the Himalayas, remembering you.

1000By your grace Agastya drank up the ocean,
and Prahlada did not die when he drank poison.

1001In the form of cloth you saved Draupadi's honour;
you gave sight to the blind Bilvamangala."

1002Hearing the blind man's words, Chaitanya Gosai
said, "Brother, why do you make me an offender?

1003Hari dwells in every heart;
ask her and see — Bhagavati will tell you.

1004What you have said is not to be heard.
Why make me an offender for nothing, brother?

1005I am an ordinary man, a lowly sinner;
your heart has fallen into the well of illusion."

1006The blind man said, "There is no more use in words;
show me your form — this is the alms I beg."

1007The blind man wept in distress for the Lord,
and the Lord went over to the blind man.

1008Seeing the blind man's devotion, beautiful Gauranga
slowly took his hand.

1009Spreading his arms, Gora embraced the blind man,
and at the Lord's touch the blind man shuddered.

[p. 93]

1010Opening his eyes as quick as lightning,
the blind man saw the Lord and was fulfilled.

1011The very moment he saw my hero of dharma,
the blind man fell and gave up his body.

1012Crying "Hari bol!" and circling the blind man,
the Lord began to dance, mad with love.

1013Having buried the blind man's body6 in that very courtyard,
Gauranga left Padmakot.

1014Leaving Padmakot, the Lord, in the town of Tripatra,7
had darshan of Shiva Chandeshvara.

1015If one cries "Bom!" in his temple,
the echo of the sound goes round for a whole danda.8

1016In that courtyard is a huge bilva tree;
everyone calls it the perfected bilva tree.

1017Many Shaivas live there,
and their leader is the most learned Bhargadeva.

1018Bhargadeva is a great scholar of philosophy;
every day he worships Hara with joy.

1019There my Lord, the son of Shachi,
closed his eyes and sang hymns with devotion.

1020Old Bhargadeva, seeing the son of Shachi,
called all the renunciants and said:

[p. 94]

1021"You have all heard of a wonderful sannyasi
who is wandering this country in quest of holy places.

1022Everyone tells of his marvellous greatness;
this is that sannyasi, the son of Shachi.

1023In his eyes there is always the shambhavi mudra;9
seeing him, no sinner or sufferer remains.

1024By the gift of the nectar of the Name he has flooded the land
and made children, women and the old drunk with the Name.

1025I have heard that he has left his own country
and come to deliver the unbelievers by giving them the Name of Hari.

1026Look, brothers, here is that young sannyasi;
this is the one everyone calls Chaitanya Gosai.

1027As I heard of him, so today I have seen him.
Ah, what a form! I have never seen anything like it.

1028This best of sannyasis is not a man;
otherwise why should my heart melt at the sight of him?

1029This person is an incarnation of God;
all of you bow down, clasping his feet."

1030Saying this, Bharga bowed down,
and the Lord bit his tongue and drew back.

1031The Lord said, "For shame, Bharga, what have you said!
My birthplace is the town of Nadia.

[p. 95]

1032I am an ordinary man, that is certain.
Why do you frighten me for nothing by calling me an avatara?

1033Why do you all again and again call me
an incarnation of God and make me an offender?

1034I have come to you on pilgrimage.
Raise your arms, brothers, say 'Hari' and dance, all of you.

1035Why make a fuss, calling me an avatara?
Come, let us all together say 'Hari, Hari bol'.

1036Never call me an incarnation of God.
You yourself are Shankara in person, lord of the world."

1037The Lord returned the obeisance with folded palms,
and Bhargadeva started up in fright.

1038Bharga rolled at his feet,
fallen on the ground, grey with dust.

1039Bharga said, "Listen, listen, Chaitanya Gosai:
have mercy on me, an old man — this is the alms I beg.

1040I know nothing of worship or spiritual practice;
I am always proud of being a detached sannyasi.

1041Go and play your tricks, Lord,
on someone who has not seen through the cunning of your lila.

1042Go to someone who has not recognised you,
and there hide your form by your stratagems.

[p. 96]

1043I am old, and because of the defect of my eyes my sight is dim;
that is why I see you as a dark-complexioned youth.10

1044People say your colour is like gold,
but this unfortunate one sees you dark, as the fruit of his fate.

1045Just once, be merciful, Chaitanya Gosai,
and show your form, if I may be granted to see it.

1046Be merciful, Lord, and give me the gift of sight;
be kind and make me fortunate.

1047If in your mercy you have shown yourself to this lowly one,
lift your foot and place it on my head."

1048Hearing the old man's words, Shachi's son
said, "Why do you make me an offender again and again?

1049I came here to see a holy man;
never mind merit, I have become a partaker of sin."

1050Hearing this, Bharga folded his hands
and said, "Take your meal here today — that is my request."

1051The Lord stayed a week in the town of Tripatra,
and many people gathered there.

1052For seven days the Lord performed Hari-sankirtana,
and everyone became drunk with the Name of Hari.

1053Many people there became Vaishnavas,
and many swung tulasi garlands round their necks.

[p. 97]

1054What more can I say about my Lord?
Wondrous is his power, marvellous his form.

1055At the end of the day Gora Raya eats a little food;
from not eating, his body is as thin as a stick.

1056He is nothing but skin and bone,
and yet the radiance of his body is like fire.

1057All are enchanted by the beauty of his body;
without any effort, the fragrance of lotus always comes from it.

1058Whoever opens his eyes and looks at him
is dazzled by the power of his effulgence.

1059After seven days, having bestowed his grace on Bharga,
my sannyasi left Tripatra.

1060Bharga follows behind as a companion;
taking Bhargadeva by the hand, he sent him back.

1061Hundreds of thousands come to see the Lord,
and the Lord never tires of giving Krishna's name.

1062No one speaks of anything but the Name of Hari;
seeing so many devotees of Krishna, all are beside themselves.

1063Everyone calls the Lord "the mad Hari-bola",11
and many cry "Hari bol!" to tease him.

1064How many people run after him crying "Hari"!
Hearing the Name, my Lord smears his body with dust.

[p. 98]

1065Gone mad with the Name of Hari, Gora-chand
now and then falls in the dust and rolls about.

1066When the Lord sent Bhargadeva away,
just then many children came to that place.

1067Someone said, "Hey, brothers, there goes that madman!
All of you shout 'Hari, Hari' and drive him wild!"

1068All the children began to tease him,
and the Lord, the son of Shachi, danced along with them.

1069Sometimes he laughs, sometimes he weeps,
sometimes he falls and drops to the ground.

1070Gradually all the people went away who knows where,
and in our path lay a vast forest.

1071There is no end to it — thickets for fifty yojanas,
and into it the son of Shachi went.

1072With no fear in my heart I walk along the footpath;
ahead goes my Chaitanya Gosai.

1073We stay under trees; there is no one there.
We satisfy our hunger by eating the fruits of the trees.

1074How can I tell how many wondrous fruits there were!
I carefully eat those fruits that surpass nectar.

1075After three days we came upon a band of sannyasis,
and I was greatly delighted.

[p. 99]

1076Joining them, we went on slowly,
and after a fortnight we came out of the forest.

1077Beyond the forest lies the pure Ranga-dhama;12
going there, the Lord gives the Name of Hari.

1078In Ranga-dhama is the image of Lord Narasimha;
seeing it, devotion arises even in an unbeliever's heart.

1079Prahlada stands before him with joined palms,
while the Lord slays the king of the demons.

1080Never have I seen such an image.
Seeing it, Chaitanya Gosai went mad.

1081The son of Shachi now falls, now rises,
now the Lord is sunk in meditation with eyes closed.

1082Seeing Nrisimha, the ocean of love surges up,
and now and then he falls crashing to the ground.

1083Sometimes the Lord, like a madman, babbles incoherently,
and foam comes from his mouth in gushes.

1084Sometimes his upper cloth is soaked with tears,
sometimes he falls to the ground, trembling.

1085Some say, "Where has this madman come from?"
Some come and fall at the Lord's feet.

1086There was a practising brahmana named Yudhishthira,
the crest-jewel of Vaishnavas, saintly in conduct.

[p. 100]

1087The brahmana worships and serves in this holy place,
and every day by reading the Gita frees himself from the fever of the world.13

1088Everyone laughs at the unlettered brahmana reading the Gita,
but the brahmana pays no heed, and that is why he was dear to the Lord.

1089He heeds no one as he studies the Gita;
setting his heart on it, he reads in solitude.

1090As long as he reads the Gita, the brahmana weeps;
seeing his tears, the Lord's heart melted.

1091The Lord said, "Why do you weep, brahmana thakura?"
The brahmana said, "When I read the Gita, I am full of joy.

1092I see Krishna on Arjuna's chariot;
for the delight of that I read the Gita, sannyasi gosai."

1093The Lord said, "You get to see Krishna —
then be kind and embrace me.

1094I have never seen a holy man like you;
by serving you I shall get to see Krishna."

1095The brahmana gazed fixedly at the Lord
and fell prostrate at the Lord's feet.

1096The Lord said, "Listen, listen, worthy brahmana:
do not tell this to anyone and everyone.

1097You are most fortunate, crest-jewel of saints;
Krishna himself shows himself to you every day."

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. A bhairavi is a female ascetic of the Shaiva or Tantric tradition.
  2. Literally "makes khish-mish", an expression of grumbling discontent.
  3. Kumbhakarna-kapara ("Kumbhakarna's skull") is a local name; the index of the 1926 edition lists Kumbhakarna-karpara.
  4. The division of lines into couplets seems to be disturbed in the edition here; the translation follows the order of the lines.
  5. Chaitanya hints that mercy should be asked of the goddess of the temple.
  6. Samadhi, the burial of a holy man (the bodies of sadhus are buried, not cremated).
  7. Tripatra is perhaps Tiruvattur or Tiruppattur; the identification is uncertain.
  8. A danda is a measure of time, 24 minutes.
  9. The shambhavi mudra is the yogic "gaze of Shambhu", in which the open eyes do not see the outer world.
  10. Govinda alludes to the traditional idea of Chaitanya as Krishna concealed by Radha's golden colour: Bharga sees him dark, like Krishna.
  11. Khepa Hari-bola, "the madman who shouts 'Hari bol'".
  12. Ranga-dhama is Srirangam.
  13. Compare the famous episode of the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9) about the illiterate brahmana at Srirangam who weeps over the Gita because he sees Krishna on Arjuna's chariot. In the Karcha this brahmana is named Yudhishthira.
